title: Police watchdog investigating after man seriously injured during arrest by Prince Albert police
subtitle: A 25-year-old man was seriously injured during his apprehension by a Prince Albert police dog on Tuesday morning.
article: The Saskatchewan Serious Incident Response Team is investigating after a 25-year-old man was seriously injured during an arrest early Tuesday morning by the Prince Albert Police Service involving a police dog.

Prince Albert city police issued a media release late Tuesday afternoon saying the man sustained the injury as a result of a "canine apprehension." Police said he was taken to Victoria Hospital in Prince Albert for treatment and was later released into police custody.
"We are fully co-operating with SIRT and as their investigation is ongoing, the PA ( sic ) Police Service is unable to comment further on this incident," the media release said.
The arrest happened after officers saw a man operating a motorcycle in a "dangerous manner" in the 400 block of River Street East around 3 a.m. on Tuesday and tried to stop it, the release said.
Police allege the man "disregarded the signal and actively tried to evade apprehension" before abandoning the motorcycle in the 200 block of Macdowall Crescent and trying to flee on foot.
In a media release Wednesday afternoon, the provincial government said Prince Albert police had been involved in a "vehicle pursuit" of a motorcycle, followed by a "brief foot pursuit."
"During the search for the operator of the motorcycle, a Police Service Dog (PSD) was deployed and the subject of the pursuit, a 25-year-old male, was seriously injured," it said.
Neither media release gave details about the man's injuries.
The provincial release said police provided first aid and called for paramedics, and that the man was released from hospital into police custody with followup medical treatment required.

The man is charged with dangerous operation of a conveyance, failure to stop for police, assault with a weapon, possession of a weapon for a dangerous purpose, carrying a concealed weapon, resisting arrest, mischief, breach of a release order, breach of probation and breach of recognizance.
He made his first court appearance in Prince Albert on Tuesday.

The province said Prince Albert police notified SIRT about the incident at 10:35 a.m. on Tuesday and a team, including the civilian executive director and four SIRT investigators, were deployed to Prince Albert "immediately."

SIRT will investigate police conduct during the incident, including the circumstances surrounding the man's arrest and the cause of his injury, while Prince Albert police will continue to investigate the man and his actions.
The province said no further information will be released at this time, but a final report will be issued to the public within 90 days of the end of the investigation.
SIRT is an independent, civilian-led team to investigate all serious incidents involving police.

It has launched two investigations into serious incidents involving Prince Albert police in 2023: the fatal police shooting of 34-year-old John Gardiner in January, and the arrest of 40-year-old Boden Umpherville in April that left him with serious injuries. Umpherville later died in hospital.
